nodes.label: Intake reproducibility (SEED 20260816)
nodes.rationale: 20,000 trials per scenario, 8,000 per ordering; percentiles 50/70/85/95; every horizon in working days beside its date.

nodes.label: What the intake forecast cannot see
nodes.norm_label: what the intake forecast cannot see
nodes.rationale: Dependencies outside the board, the t-shirt judgement itself, work not yet raised, whether the ask is worth doing, ramp-up. Restated in every brief because a forecast that hides its blind spots is worse than none.

nodes.label: PINNED data residency without a remote
nodes.norm_label: pinned data residency without a remote
nodes.rationale: An app whose in-scope data lives only in Forge hosted storage qualifies for PINNED without configuration. Removing a remotes entry is a minor version; adding one or changing baseUrl is major.

nodes.label: Distroless is not a minimal CVE surface for Python
nodes.norm_label: distroless is not a minimal cve surface for python
nodes.rationale: distroless/python3-debian12 scanned at 46 HIGH/CRITICAL with 18 fixable; it answers 'ship no shell' not 'carry fewer CVEs'.

nodes.norm_label: adr 0016: the image takes debian's security updates at build time

nodes.label: The image applies Debian security updates at build time
nodes.norm_label: the image applies debian security updates at build time
nodes.rationale: On 2026-08-28 the scan gate blocked every deploy on CVE-2026-14456 in OpenSSL (3 fixable findings). Rebuilding, pinning a newer digest and swapping base (3.13-slim, alpine, distroless) were all measured and all failed on the same CVE because no distribution had rebuilt for it. apt-get upgrade (never dist-upgrade) as the first layer: 3 fixable before, 0 after, image 52.6 to 56.5 MB.

nodes.label: Scan gate: fixable HIGH/CRITICAL block; unfixable are reported
nodes.norm_label: scan gate: fixable high/critical block; unfixable are reported
nodes.rationale: The line is actionability, not severity, because a gate that blocks on things no merge can fix is one people route around. Loosening the gate and suppressing via .trivyignore were refused: the first fixable finding waved through with a good reason is the point the gate becomes advisory. A red scan was twice misdescribed as unfixable findings by people who had not run service/scan.sh.

nodes.label: Board
nodes.rationale: The delivery unit a forecast is scoped to; throughput, interruption rate and t-shirt scale never transfer between boards. Exactly two kinds.

nodes.label: Bundle
nodes.rationale: Several contexts and their issues in one file, fetched up front so switching is instant and offline.

nodes.label: Cumulative flow
nodes.rationale: Items per status category per day, three bands because nothing records which column an issue sat in.

nodes.label: Cycle time
nodes.rationale: Started to resolved, the part actively worked.

nodes.label: Flow board
nodes.rationale: Runs no sprints; detected rather than declared because Jira answers 400 for its sprint list.

nodes.label: Flow health
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency at 40% weight, blockers and ageing at 30% each; refuses outright without flow efficiency because the remainder is hygiene.

nodes.label: Health score
nodes.rationale: A weighted band that always shows its working; two of them, one per board kind, never the same quantity.

nodes.label: Lead time
nodes.rationale: Created to resolved, the whole wait.

nodes.label: Period
nodes.rationale: Whichever of sprint or window a context is bounded by; the word for sentences true of both.

nodes.label: Context (selected)
nodes.rationale: One project + board + period; its kind is sent rather than inferred from the id shape.

nodes.label: Sprint
nodes.rationale: Both a bound and a clock: fixed scope with a start and end delivery is measured against.

nodes.label: Sprint board
nodes.rationale: The only board kind with a committed scope and a clock, hence the only one with a burndown, pace and sprint health.

nodes.label: Sprint health
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace, scope stability, blockers, ageing; two need a clock so it is replaced on a flow board.

nodes.label: Waiting
nodes.rationale: Lead time minus cycle time; most of the total on typical data and the cheapest thing to fix.

nodes.label: Window
nodes.rationale: Rolling stretch of calendar days on a flow board; a bound and not a clock, carrying no working-day list because a team that committed to nothing cannot be behind.

nodes.label: Fetcher with an API token (scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py)
nodes.rationale: Right for your own board, wrong for a customer's: the token carries its owner's permissions, cannot be scoped, and is revoked only by deletion. Carries previous values forward and prints what was missing.

nodes.label: MCP connectors and CSV export routes
nodes.norm_label: mcp connectors and csv export routes
nodes.rationale: Claude holds the MCP connection, not the page; CSV export is the right starting point to prove which metrics people use before building a pipeline.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) route via scripts/jira_auth.py
nodes.rationale: Read-only scopes read:jira-work and read:jira-user, callback on 127.0.0.1:8721, grant stored in .jira-oauth.json mode 0600 and git-ignored; a grant covering several sites makes the fetcher refuse to guess. --auth auto prefers the grant and prints which was used.

nodes.label: Calculator
nodes.rationale: The hosted service that ran agent/tools/ unchanged for the Forge app; retired by ADR 0031, after which the same Python runs inside the Forge function.

nodes.label: Conditions that would revive impersonation
nodes.rationale: If the brief ever names an issue (checked in tests); if a customer runs issue-level security and says so; if the app is distributed through the Marketplace.

nodes.label: problemsInAuditEntry: counts, flags, field names, one actor identity
nodes.norm_label: problemsinauditentry: counts, flags, field names, one actor identity
nodes.rationale: The actor is unavoidable; a recipient's account id cannot reach a store that grows without bound. Writing never fails the act it records. Administrators only, gated by canEdit.

nodes.label: orgConfig.countSubtasks (default false)
nodes.rationale: Subtasks inflate item counts by decomposition habit exactly as points inflate by estimation; whether subtasks even arrive varies by board type and route, so the product could not say what its counts included. Uses Jira's issuetype.subtask flag, never the type name; absent means not a subtask.

nodes.label: orgConfig.countedTypes allow-list (default empty)
nodes.rationale: Empty means every type the subtask rule left; naming types per site means a new type silently stops counting.

nodes.label: orgConfig.valueFromHierarchy (default 1)
nodes.rationale: Value counted at epic level and above only: an epic worth £40k with five £8k stories is one value and six rows. A level rather than a type list so a site adding 'Initiative' keeps counting; issues with no recorded level still count.

nodes.label: orgConfig.askField
nodes.rationale: 'app' reads the declared Candidate field; any other value names a site field matched by id then display name — an instruction, not a guess, unlike findBusinessValueField.

nodes.label: candidate_answer: None / True / False / str
nodes.rationale: None is silence (a band may speak), True yes, False no (beats a band), str an unreadable answer reported with the words written. None-vs-False is load-bearing: the first amendment read 'is not False' and made every epic a candidate.

nodes.label: MIN_TSHIRT_EPICS = 8 (vs MIN_REFERENCE_EPICS 5)
nodes.rationale: History split four ways needs more observations; a board below it refuses in those words and the ask appears in skipped.

nodes.label: orgConfig.sizeField
nodes.rationale: Points at a site's own size field, recommended because Forge cannot declare a select.

nodes.label: orgConfig block, a sibling of meta
nodes.norm_label: orgconfig block, a sibling of meta
nodes.rationale: Done/in-progress statuses, working week, holidays, sprint length, resolved once by the producer and written into the file so tools and page cannot describe one sprint under two calendars; absent means the old hard-coded defaults.

nodes.label: Refusal thresholds
nodes.rationale: Completion forecast >=10 completed items and >=8 day-observations, named separately with units; cycle-time risk >=6 items; calibration >=10 resolved; reference class >=5 epics; t-shirt >=8; explicit min<=likely<=max; sequencing >=2 sizeable asks.

nodes.label: ADR 0020: The anchor issue is the brief's access control, and impersonation is deferred
nodes.norm_label: adr 0020: the anchor issue is the brief's access control, and impersonation is deferred

nodes.label: ADR 0021: The audit log is operational, and says so
nodes.norm_label: adr 0021: the audit log is operational, and says so

nodes.label: ADR 0024 A parent and its subtasks are one piece of work
nodes.norm_label: adr 0024 a parent and its subtasks are one piece of work

nodes.label: ADR 0025 The app declares a Business Value field
nodes.norm_label: adr 0025 the app declares a business value field

nodes.label: ADR 0026 Items and value are counted from two different sets
nodes.norm_label: adr 0026 items and value are counted from two different sets

nodes.label: ADR 0028 Candidacy is a state somebody declares
nodes.norm_label: adr 0028 candidacy is a state somebody declares

nodes.label: ADR 0029 A t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.norm_label: adr 0029 a t-shirt band selects a reference class

nodes.label: Administer Jira global permission refused
nodes.rationale: permissions/check for another user needs it, it is the largest grant discussed anywhere in the repository, and the endpoint's own docs say the answer may not hold for all issues anyway. Refused again in ADR 0021 for reading Jira's audit log.

nodes.label: Offline user impersonation (asUser(accountId), allowImpersonation) is deferred, not rejected
nodes.norm_label: offline user impersonation (asuser(accountid), allowimpersonation) is deferred, not rejected
nodes.rationale: ADR 0018 called per-recipient composition 'a different product'; that was written from memory and is wrong — Forge documents it, with a scheduled trigger as the motivating case. Deferred because an app not on the Marketplace can only impersonate contributors, every send multiplies, and trigger-runtime support is unverified. tests/test_service.py fails if allowImpersonation appears without revisiting this record.

nodes.label: An app writing its own rewritable log is not tamper-evident
nodes.norm_label: an app writing its own rewritable log is not tamper-evident
nodes.rationale: A tile presenting it as an audit trail would be the most convincing wrong thing in the product; the route that answers a security review is emitting events to the customer's own sink, a bigger crossing than ADR 0013 and a separate record. The word 'audit' without qualification is ruled out everywhere.

nodes.label: Build the operational log; say plainly it is not a compliance record
nodes.norm_label: build the operational log; say plainly it is not a compliance record
nodes.rationale: Most of an audit log never depended on item 5: recipient changes and brief sends are acts of this app under an authority already enforced. Jira accepts no audit record from an app and reading Jira's own log needs Administer Jira. forge/src/audit.js holds four events (recipients.saved, recipients.cleared, brief.sent, brief.refused) in app storage; the tile and auditNote say it is not tamper-evident and tests assert they still do.

nodes.label: facts.meta.counting / forecast.inputs.counting
nodes.rationale: Reports seen, counted and not counted whether or not anything was excluded; a key present only sometimes reads as nothing when absent.

nodes.label: Reader's issue-type filter
nodes.rationale: Lists types the board actually uses; narrows the organisation's rule and never widens it (expressed as an effective config so counted_issues stays the one implementation); travels with the forecast request and cache key; selecting nothing is a refusal per ADR 0010.

nodes.label: Major vs minor Forge version rule
nodes.norm_label: major vs minor forge version rule
nodes.rationale: Correction: introducing a module type or changing a scope is major; adding an entry under an already-declared block is minor (ADR 0027's field deployed as 7.2.0 with no MAJOR_VERSION_RULE approval). Checked by deploying, not reasoning.

nodes.label: Three empty states of the value tile
nodes.norm_label: three empty states of the value tile
nodes.rationale: Nothing priced; nothing priced at the counted level; field not on a screen (the state every install is in on upgrade day). Each names its own fix.

nodes.label: Epics are fetched separately
nodes.rationale: Epic issues do not belong to scrum boards, so the sprint issue endpoint never returned the thing value was recorded on; listed from /board/{id}/epic (scope read:epic:jira-software) and credited to the period they resolved in.

nodes.label: counted_issues vs value_issues: two sets
nodes.rationale: An epic is a container of items (excluded from item counts like a subtask) and the only place value lives, so one filtered list cannot serve both. Getting it wrong printed '-1 of the 0 completed items' and threw on click-through; pinned in tests/e2e.py.

nodes.label: Candidacy is a state, not a type
nodes.norm_label: candidacy is a state, not a type
nodes.rationale: A committed, half-built epic is not being weighed; sequencing it would look like advice. A type is permanent, candidacy becomes true and stops being true, so somebody has to say it.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band declares candidacy (amendment)
nodes.rationale: Reverses the refusal to infer, for one field only: four screen configurations before a feature works is what an evaluation meets first, and choosing a size is already a statement about work being weighed. CANDIDATE_NO makes it reversible out loud.

nodes.label: sizing_method / sizing_basis on every ordering row
nodes.norm_label: sizing_method / sizing_basis on every ordering row
nodes.rationale: Banded and unbanded asks share one comparison and the 'Sized by' column says which; all-or-nothing per board and sequencing only the sized asks were both rejected as silent narrowing.

nodes.label: requests>=2.31 (fetcher's only dependency)
nodes.rationale: The security suite asserts the fetcher's dependency list stays at one, because the fetcher holds a customer's credentials.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: The dashboard is one self-contained HTML file
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: the dashboard is one self-contained html file

nodes.label: ADR 0022: SSO is inherited, because this app owns no identity
nodes.norm_label: adr 0022: sso is inherited, because this app owns no identity

nodes.label: Threat model: the file gets emailed
nodes.norm_label: threat model: the file gets emailed
nodes.rationale: The file leaves the building; zero network and zero browser storage are enforced by the security suite so nothing in it can phone home or leak.

nodes.label: Single self-contained HTML file
nodes.rationale: Executives will not install anything and engineers will not trust a number they cannot open; a file with no build step, server, dependencies, network calls or storage satisfies both and survives being forwarded as an email attachment. The cost (no npm, hand-rolled SVG charts, committed dist/) was accepted because every dependency either phones home or fails to load once the file leaves the building.

nodes.label: Forge CSP forbids inline style/script; split build and CSSOM setter wrap
nodes.norm_label: forge csp forbids inline style/script; split build and cssom setter wrap
nodes.rationale: A Forge Custom UI iframe blocks inline <style>, <script> and style= attributes silently. build.py --split emits the same sources as linked assets (one assembly declining to inline, not a second implementation). Relaxing the CSP via permissions.content.styles unsafe-inline was rejected; removing style= attributes was rejected because it would make the single file's layout depend on JavaScript. src/app.js feature-detects the discarded attribute and wraps the innerHTML setter once, because a missed call site is a tile that silently loses its colour.

nodes.label: No Atlassian credential, session or auth module in the app
nodes.norm_label: no atlassian credential, session or auth module in the app
nodes.rationale: A hard Marketplace requirement: an app holding a user's API token makes its REST activity indistinguishable from the customer's own and holds a credential no IdP can see. process.env appears in index.js once, in a comment; the check reads code not prose because an earlier suite failed on a comment (the dist-upgrade mistake).

nodes.label: The personal API token path lives only in scripts/
nodes.norm_label: the personal api token path lives only in scripts/
nodes.rationale: scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py can use JIRA_TOKEN, a credential no IdP stands in front of. It is an operator's tool on their own machine and the suite asserts it exists only in scripts/. If a supported route is ever chosen, OAuth (scripts/jira_auth.py) is the one to keep.

nodes.label: SSO is inherited because the app owns no identity
nodes.norm_label: sso is inherited because the app owns no identity
nodes.rationale: The panel is authenticated by Atlassian (context.accountId), the calculator authenticates callers not people, and the built file is a file with nobody to authenticate. Nothing to build — the same shape residency took under ADR 0012. Falsifiable claims are enforced by sso_checks() in tests/security.py. Not a claim of compliance, not a claim that authorisation (item 5) is solved.

nodes.label: Pyodide in the Custom UI iframe
nodes.norm_label: pyodide in the custom ui iframe
nodes.rationale: A .wasm from the app's own static resource is not egress, but WebAssembly compilation needs unsafe-eval in permissions.content.scripts (a major version) and the scheduled weekly brief has no browser to run in, so it is at most half an answer.

nodes.label: unsafe-eval CSP option for WebAssembly
nodes.rationale: wasm-unsafe-eval is not an allowed value; the community reports unsafe-eval working for a Custom UI in 2023. Adding a CSP option is a major version.

nodes.label: meta.calendar must equal inputs.calendar
nodes.rationale: Both tools report the calendar from the dataset's orgConfig; if they differ the two tools read different files and nothing is comparable.

nodes.label: assertAsksCarryNoText / _refuse_ask_text
nodes.rationale: Asks are built, not projected through the allow-list, so /v1/sequence and /v1/ask accepted a title until this guard.

nodes.label: What counts as a finished epic
nodes.norm_label: what counts as a finished epic
nodes.rationale: Stopped growing (no item created in 30 days), at least 90% complete, at least three items; thresholds are arguments to epic_sizes().

nodes.label: The sizing ladder (tshirt / reference-class / explicit)
nodes.rationale: Three methods in increasing order of evidence; the tool records which was used and prints its caveat verbatim, because the caveat is what stops the number being over-read.

nodes.label: T-shirt sizes calibrated per board
nodes.rationale: An organisation-wide scale is a fiction; S/M/L/XL are quartiles of the board's own completed epics. Fewer than eight completed epics is a refusal since four quartiles from seven observations are noise wearing a uniform. The range reflects variance within a band, not the risk of the wrong band.

nodes.label: Async event at-least-once delivery and retries
nodes.norm_label: async event at-least-once delivery and retries
nodes.rationale: 200 KB per push (100 KB per event above 55 s timeout), 50 events per push, 500 per minute; a timeout is an app-level error retried within a 24 h retention window with exponential backoff; retryContext carries retryCount, retryReason, retryData, retentionWindow.

nodes.label: Consumer function limits: 900 s, 1,024 MB
nodes.rationale: timeoutSeconds 1-900 applies to scheduled triggers and async consumers only, default 55 s; memory 512 MB default, 1,024 MB max, per function. Billing is measured time, so a smaller timeout bounds a hung run.

nodes.label: Forge consumer module
nodes.rationale: modules.consumer[] with key, queue, function, optional crossVersion; the named function carries its own timeoutSeconds and memoryMB. Queue name in the manifest is the one passed to new Queue({key}).

nodes.label: Forge Realtime as an alternative to polling
nodes.norm_label: forge realtime as an alternative to polling
nodes.rationale: GA, 50 ops/s per installation, no scope; from a consumer only subscribeGlobal/publishGlobal work and a page that navigated away misses the answer unless it is also in storage.

nodes.label: Job status is counts only; cancel exists
nodes.norm_label: job status is counts only; cancel exists
nodes.rationale: push returns jobId; getJob(jobId).cancel() and getStats() returning {success, inProgress, failed} are the whole documented status, so the result itself must be written to storage; delayInSeconds up to 15 minutes.

nodes.label: KVS as the result store for a poller
nodes.norm_label: kvs as the result store for a poller
nodes.rationale: storage:app already declared; 240 KiB per value, 500-char keys, 4,000 reads and writes per minute per installation, TTL up to a year, kvs.get strictly consistent. No index or query needed since the page knows the jobId.

nodes.label: Documented major-version change list
nodes.rationale: Scopes, CSP options, external URLs, dynamic web triggers, egress categories, inScopeEUD, licensing, providers, remotes, customer-managed egress; everything else minor. Not presented as exhaustive; the repository saw jira:customField go major, so the CLI on deploy is the arbiter.

nodes.label: CPython WASI as an alternative
nodes.rationale: Tier 2 platform, 14-15 MB zipped unofficial builds, Node's node:wasi is experimental; no smaller than Pyodide and weaker.

nodes.label: Local Pyodide measurement on M3 Pro
nodes.norm_label: local pyodide measurement on m3 pro
nodes.rationale: loadPyodide 0.98 s, FC.build 0.37-0.41 s, IN.sequence 4 asks 4.08 s, all byte-identical to native across CPython 3.9, 3.14, Node and Chrome; a backgrounded tab more than doubles the time.

nodes.label: Pyodide inside a Forge function
nodes.rationale: WebAssembly instantiates in the native Node runtime; a warm container keeps the loaded runtime so the 6.8 s cold load is paid once per container. Facts/forecast 1.3-1.5 s warm; sequencing 13.6 s warm, ~21 s cold, against a 25 s resolver timeout.

nodes.label: Runs on Atlassian eligibility criteria
nodes.rationale: Atlassian-hosted compute and storage only, matching data residency, customer-controlled egress. Eligible apps list no external resource domains, remotes, Connect modules, providers or dynamic web triggers; the analytics exception is narrow.

nodes.label: The wasm-probe throwaway app experiment
nodes.rationale: webtrigger template, nodejs24.x, memoryMB 1024, arm64; five tools, datasets and Pyodide 314.0.6 runtime files as base64 in the bundle, unpacked to /tmp. 17.7 MB zip deployed; the only eligibility finding was the template's dynamic web trigger.

nodes.label: Adding a consumer is a minor version; a remote is major
nodes.norm_label: adding a consumer is a minor version; a remote is major
nodes.rationale: 2.0.0 to 2.1.0 on adding consumer, function and timeoutSeconds 300; raising to 900 also minor. Adding a remote stopped for --approve MAJOR_VERSION_RULE (data residency or egress modification); removing it was minor. Settled by deploy, the rule CLAUDE.md sets.

nodes.label: A timed-out consumer retries in about 40 seconds
nodes.norm_label: a timed-out consumer retries in about 40 seconds
nodes.rationale: Not the fifteen-minute ceiling documented; retryContext arrives; getJob().cancel() stopped it; getStats() reported zeros mid-retry and is no use as a status source. The retry guard is more urgent than ADR 0031 said.

nodes.label: Forecast barely grows with board size
nodes.norm_label: forecast barely grows with board size
nodes.rationale: route_forecast 1.52 s at 480 issues, 2.78 s at 4,800; route_facts 0.30 s and 2.49 s; the service's validation layer imports under Pyodide unchanged.

nodes.label: Pyodide memory snapshot trade-off
nodes.rationale: makeMemorySnapshot cuts cold start from 11 s to 1.3 s but costs 1.65x on every computation afterwards, measured A/B in one container; Forge's runtime, not Pyodide's. Suits the synchronous resolver function, not the consumer.

nodes.label: wasm-probe-2 throwaway app
nodes.rationale: Node v24.18.0 arm64, memoryMB 1024, Pyodide 314.0.6 with the tools, service/app.py, two datasets, fifty asks and a 30 MB snapshot in a 17.0 MB assets.js; every SHA-256 matched native Python 3.14.7. Installation f52bde9e on the dev site, version 3.2.0.

nodes.label: Research note: async events for sequencing (2026-09-01)
nodes.norm_label: research note: async events for sequencing (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Can a Custom UI resolver with a 25 s budget hand a ~170 s sequencing job to an async event and collect it later? Every claim labelled documented or not established; no experiment run.

nodes.label: Research note: recovering the Runs on Atlassian badge (2026-09-01)
nodes.norm_label: research note: recovering the runs on atlassian badge (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Can the app have the badge while running agent/tools/ unchanged? Keeping the Cloud Run calculator: blocked. Pyodide in a Forge function: works, measured on a throwaway app, byte-identical figures, ten times native CPU.

nodes.label: Research note: the second probe (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: What the platform did, as opposed to what the documentation says: consumer versioning, cubic sequencing, memory snapshot cost, retry timing, storage TTL.

nodes.label: Epic grouping field chosen once for the whole set
nodes.norm_label: epic grouping field chosen once for the whole set

nodes.label: A resolver returns before its pushed work completes
nodes.norm_label: a resolver returns before its pushed work completes

nodes.rationale: Webpack shipped only .cjs output and rewrote Pyodide's dynamic import into a lazy namespace that fails, which is why the runtime files travel as base64 and load from /tmp.

nodes.label: Declaring a remote costs eligibility before any traffic
nodes.norm_label: declaring a remote costs eligibility before any traffic

nodes.rationale: A set of dated percentiles from simulating throughput against remaining work; never a single date.

nodes.norm_label: started date lives in the changelog, not the export
nodes.rationale: A CSV cannot give when work started; without it there is no cycle time. Use a Development-started field or scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py which derives it from the changelog.

nodes.norm_label: business value delivered ($34,800 estimated, with stated basis)

nodes.norm_label: value basis as prose (conversion uplift: 2.1% of 41k monthly sessions x $40 aov)
