nodes.norm_label: value is a floor, not a total (items without a stated basis count as zero)

nodes.label: Evidence tagging
nodes.rationale: [measured], [derived], [forecast pNN], [judgement]; a section reaching three judgements in a row is cut.

nodes.label: Prohibited outputs
nodes.rationale: Computing any number, single-point dates, per-person ranking, forecasts without percentile and scope assumption, restating an unchanged report, softening a refusal, any priority score, t-shirt dates as commitments, any recommendation to work longer.

nodes.label: Agent refusal thresholds
nodes.rationale: Fewer than 10 completed items, 5 finished epics for reference class, 8 for a t-shirt scale, 6 items with start and end dates, no previous snapshot, Brier above 0.20.

nodes.label: Agent sequence: load, diff, forecast, reconcile, write, log, score
nodes.norm_label: agent sequence: load, diff, forecast, reconcile, write, log, score
nodes.rationale: metrics.py first so meta.as_of fixes the date; movement is the news; refusals verbatim; disagreements are usually units; log every probability; score calibration at ten resolved entries.

nodes.label: Cycle time percentile
nodes.rationale: What 50/85/95% of finished items came in under; the 85th is quoted outward as a statement about the system, never one item.

nodes.label: Diff
nodes.rationale: The change between two snapshots with the direction that counts as good stated per figure.

nodes.label: Elapsed time
nodes.rationale: Time as a stakeholder experiences it, always calendar days.

nodes.label: Facts pack
nodes.rationale: The complete set of figures a report may state, computed once and quoted verbatim.

nodes.label: Refusal
nodes.rationale: The answer when evidence falls below a threshold, stating what was needed and what was there; quoted word for word.

nodes.label: Simulated time
nodes.rationale: Time inside a forecast, always working days; never reported without its unit.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: A facts pack stored with its date so a later report can say what changed.

nodes.label: Sprint 24 delivery brief (worked example)
nodes.rationale: Storefront Team as at 10 August 2026: 0.4% chance of all ten items by 14 August, p85 26 August, v2.2.0 decision needed by Wednesday; every figure tagged and from metrics.py/forecast.py.

nodes.label: Sprint 24 team report (worked example)
nodes.rationale: 12/22 items, BLC-429 to unblock first, four never-started items as realistic carry-over, commit 11 items at p85, size-stability safe, ownership counts only.

nodes.label: delivery-report agent skill
nodes.rationale: Turns a dataset into an executive brief and a team report and forecasts outstanding work; calls tools for every number and writes for two audiences.

nodes.label: Exec brief template
nodes.rationale: Will we make it, what changed, what it is worth, the decision needed; under 400 words; 'Nothing needed from you this week' rather than an invented decision; calibration footer.

nodes.label: Team report template
nodes.rationale: Where we are, forecast in working days, unblock first, ageing on two clocks, flow, what to commit next from recommend_commitment at 85%, size-stability check, open by owner with no ranking.

nodes.label: team_slice de-duplicates issues by key
nodes.rationale: A flow board's three windows hold the same issues, so every issue was in the slice three times and the 85th percentile came back two and a half times too early. A plausible wrong number, not a failure.

nodes.label: restrict: BROWSE filters recipients against the anchor issue only
nodes.norm_label: restrict: browse filters recipients against the anchor issue only
nodes.rationale: Permission filtering enforced by the platform rather than asserted by the app, but partial: it restricts against the one issue the notification hangs off, not every issue the brief counts.

nodes.label: The brief's prompt is a list of numbers, not titles
nodes.norm_label: the brief's prompt is a list of numbers, not titles
nodes.rationale: Every section in sectionsFor is counts, dates and units and briefMessages hands the model only those; the roadmap and ADR 0013 overstate what the model is given.

nodes.label: The three places mirroring does not hold
nodes.norm_label: the three places mirroring does not hold
nodes.rationale: 1) the durable series stores rows fetched as one viewer and shows them to everyone; 2) the forecast log has the same shape; 3) the brief tells recipients aggregates over issues they may not browse (restrict is anchor-only). All three leak counts, never identity.

nodes.label: ADR 0013: The brief is written inside the tenant; only the file leaves
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013: the brief is written inside the tenant; only the file leaves

nodes.label: ADR 0014: Jira sends the brief, and the read-only rule bends by allow-list
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014: jira sends the brief, and the read-only rule bends by allow-list

nodes.label: ADR 0018: Permission mirroring holds by accident, and here is where it does not
nodes.norm_label: adr 0018: permission mirroring holds by accident, and here is where it does not

nodes.label: Superseded in part: the scheduled read takes asApp() deliberately
nodes.norm_label: superseded in part: the scheduled read takes asapp() deliberately
nodes.rationale: What changed is restrict: ADR 0014 put the send through Jira with restrict BROWSE, so who may receive is the platform's decision. Residual risk: restrict filters against the anchor issue, not the issues named. Authority is an explicit parameter defaulting to user; the recipient-editor permission check and the connection probe may never take 'app', asserted structurally.

nodes.label: The file leaves: mailing is the one boundary crossing (later closed by ADR 0014)
nodes.norm_label: the file leaves: mailing is the one boundary crossing (later closed by adr 0014)
nodes.rationale: Slack was rejected (an attachment nobody opens, becoming a link); letting the calculator build the file was rejected because clean_dataset() refuses free text and rendering there inverts the service's argument.

nodes.label: The brief is written by Forge LLMs in Atlassian's runtime
nodes.norm_label: the brief is written by forge llms in atlassian's runtime
nodes.rationale: agent/SKILL.md needs a model and a third-party endpoint would put every issue title through a provider the customer has no relationship with, weekly. @forge/llm (GA July 2026) calls Atlassian-hosted Claude with no egress; declared as a module, a major version. Projecting titles away before prompting was rejected because inside Atlassian's runtime there is no crossing to protect and a brief without titles cannot say which work is stuck.

nodes.label: A scheduled trigger runs with no user principal
nodes.norm_label: a scheduled trigger runs with no user principal
nodes.rationale: Every panel read is api.asUser(), which is roadmap item 5 (permission mirroring) holding for free. A mailed brief read asApp() asserts every recipient may see every issue. So item 3 depends on item 5, which the roadmap did not say; the trigger initially refused rather than reach for asApp().

nodes.label: forge/src/compose.js keeps the send provable without deploying
nodes.norm_label: forge/src/compose.js keeps the send provable without deploying
nodes.rationale: index.js imports the Forge SDK and cannot load outside Atlassian's runtime; the code deciding what reaches an inbox has the model and the send injected so tests supply stubs.

nodes.label: Jira sends the brief via issue notify; nothing leaves
nodes.norm_label: jira sends the brief via issue notify; nothing leaves
nodes.rationale: POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/notify sends mail through Jira's own machinery, so item 3 crosses no boundary. Recipients are Jira identities never addresses (a config leak discloses interest, not contact details); restrict drops recipients who lack BROWSE on the anchor at send time; no attachments, so the two views ship as static HTML in the body rather than the self-contained file.

nodes.label: Outgoing mail is a site setting, not a scope
nodes.norm_label: outgoing mail is a site setting, not a scope
nodes.rationale: Proved 2026-08-26: 'Outgoing emails disabled' 403. sendBrief quotes Jira's errorMessages because a bare 403 is indistinguishable between three fixes; the precondition belongs in the Marketplace listing.

nodes.label: People picker searches by name, stores the id, projects to an allow-list of fields
nodes.norm_label: people picker searches by name, stores the id, projects to an allow-list of fields
nodes.rationale: Nobody knows colleagues' account ids. The app never maps an email to an account (an identity claim it has no standing to make); a human picks from Jira's matches, searched as the reader. user/search returns emailAddress etc., so people.js builds each match from an allow-list of two fields — a deny-list is one Atlassian release from leaking. Stored ids resolve back to names with a third field, state, because live, deactivated and missing have different fixes.

nodes.label: Project administrators decide who receives a board
nodes.norm_label: project administrators decide who receives a board
nodes.rationale: A recipient list is a disclosure control, not a display preference. Checked against Jira's own /mypermissions ADMINISTER_PROJECTS answer. Site admins were rejected because putting one person between every team and their board is how a feature stays switched off.

nodes.label: The read-only rule becomes an allow-list with justifications
nodes.norm_label: the read-only rule becomes an allow-list with justifications
nodes.rationale: startswith('read:') in tests/test_service.py could not admit send:notification:jira and storage:app. Neither is write access to customer data. The test now lists permitted scopes and every non-read entry must carry a written justification; adding a scope stays a deliberate edit with a reason. Writing config to a Jira project property was rejected because it needs a write scope into Jira.

nodes.label: Every app-level store is declared in tests/test_service.py with its authority
nodes.norm_label: every app-level store is declared in tests/test_service.py with its authority
nodes.rationale: The exposure is an inventory, not a hunt — the same shape as the non-read scope allow-list, so a fourth store cannot appear silently.

nodes.label: Permission mirroring holds for free because every panel read is asUser()
nodes.norm_label: permission mirroring holds for free because every panel read is asuser()
nodes.rationale: Jira decides what comes back, so no figure was computed over an issue the viewer cannot browse. Not a mechanism this product built; it costs nothing as long as nothing is kept — and item 4a converted that property into an assumption.

nodes.label: The anchor issue is the brief's access control
nodes.norm_label: the anchor issue is the brief's access control
nodes.rationale: Names the mechanism that already exists: the administrator picks the anchor, Jira enforces BROWSE on it at send time. The residual aggregate leak is accepted for ADR 0019's reasons plus one more: a brief recipient has been vouched for twice (administrator and Jira), a panel reader once, so answering this more strictly than the stores would be incoherent.

nodes.label: Refusal clause: the evidence is absent, not noisy
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause: the evidence is absent, not noisy
nodes.rationale: Every refusal sentence ends with this clause; it is the point of the refusal and must not be trimmed. Refusals are printed verbatim by the agent, never softened.

nodes.label: Flow health replaces the sprint-health chip
nodes.norm_label: flow health replaces the sprint-health chip
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency 40%, blockers 30%, ageing 30% through the same composition machinery; the chip names which composite it carries and refuses outright without flow efficiency because what survives is hygiene.

nodes.label: ADR 0007: Below the evidence thresholds, refuse rather than widen the interval
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007: below the evidence thresholds, refuse rather than widen the interval

nodes.label: ADR 0010: An empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: an empty selection is a refusal, not a zero

nodes.label: ADR 0011: A kanban context is a window, and a window is not a clock
nodes.norm_label: adr 0011: a kanban context is a window, and a window is not a clock

nodes.label: Refuse rather than widen the interval
nodes.norm_label: refuse rather than widen the interval
nodes.rationale: A wide interval says 'we know this is variable'; a refusal says 'we do not know this at all'. Below the threshold only the refusal is true, and the wide interval is more dangerous because it still carries a quotable number. Thresholds are hard, not advisory.

nodes.label: A composite drops an unmeasurable component and names it
nodes.norm_label: a composite drops an unmeasurable component and names it
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace (0.34 weight) scored 0/100 for unknown sprint dates and turned Amber to Red. A component that could not be measured is dropped, survivors re-weighted, and the chip says '3 of 4 measures' with the actual weights — the no-silent-caps rule. Scoring the gap zero or a neutral 0.5 was rejected.

nodes.label: An empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.norm_label: an empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.rationale: Over zero issues a share has no denominator and divide-by-zero guards (Math.max(items.length,1), ? ... : 0) return good news; the health score printed 'Needs attention (66/100)' for a page with nothing on it, which is the state the Forge build opens in. Tiles that would state a figure refuse in the tools' own words; honest nil counts keep their nil.

nodes.label: Below half the weight the composite refuses
nodes.norm_label: below half the weight the composite refuses
nodes.rationale: In points over an unestimated dataset both volume components are undefined; what survives is hygiene, which cannot carry the name 'sprint health'.

nodes.label: A single 'no data' banner and dimming were rejected
nodes.norm_label: a single 'no data' banner and dimming were rejected
nodes.rationale: A banner throws away what the page still knows (zero issues, which tiles already refuse for their own reasons); fading to 0.45 opacity put the only text below the AA contrast floor once tiles state their condition in words.

nodes.label: A kanban context is a rolling window
nodes.norm_label: a kanban context is a rolling window
nodes.rationale: A board with no sprints gets a window: a bounded, reproducible stretch of calendar days holding the issues open at the as-of date plus those resolved inside it, round-tripping through an id like PROJ/42/win:30d. The board unbounded, a release/epic boundary, a synthetic sprint and a mixed rollup were all rejected.

nodes.label: A tile that can never say anything is not shown
nodes.norm_label: a tile that can never say anything is not shown
nodes.rationale: Burndown, commitment history and team load have no subject on a flow board; three permanent apologies become furniture. They are disabled in the tile picker with the reason, and the reader's selection is masked not edited.

nodes.label: Window membership: open at as-of plus resolved inside
nodes.norm_label: window membership: open at as-of plus resolved inside
nodes.rationale: This set keeps ageing and WIP (which resolved-only loses) and is reproducible from the schema (which 'anything touched' is not). Cost: Delivered % has no denominator and refuses, because done/total over a set defined partly by being done rises when the window widens.

nodes.label: A window is not a clock
nodes.norm_label: a window is not a clock
nodes.rationale: A sprint is both a bound and a clock; a window supplies only the bound. Expanding its dates into working days would print 'Pace vs clock: -18 pp' for a team that never committed to anything — arithmetically correct and about nothing. So the window carries no working-day list and pace, scope growth, burndown and sprint health refuse. It is a second caller of contextWorkingDays()'s rollup rule, not a new mechanism.

nodes.label: Refusal sentences are inserted verbatim, not passed through the model
nodes.norm_label: refusal sentences are inserted verbatim, not passed through the model
nodes.rationale: A model asked to write readable prose around 'too little completion history' will paraphrase it into something that sounds like a wide interval, which is exactly what ADR 0007 forbids.

nodes.label: A refusal is not a claim
nodes.norm_label: a refusal is not a claim
nodes.rationale: Recording a refusal as a prediction would score the forecaster on answers it explicitly refused to give, inverting the point of refusing.

nodes.label: The bound is cumulative and visible: droppedTotal lives in the store
nodes.norm_label: the bound is cumulative and visible: droppedtotal lives in the store
nodes.rationale: A reader arriving after the ten-thousandth event is told nine thousand rows are gone; an audit log that silently forgets is worse than none because the absence of a row reads as the absence of the event.

nodes.label: Live mode
nodes.rationale: An optional local server the page discovers to pull contexts the bundle lacks; not a connection to the tracker.

nodes.label: Single-context repo: CONTEXT.md and docs/adr at the root
nodes.norm_label: single-context repo: context.md and docs/adr at the root
nodes.rationale: Read the glossary and relevant ADRs before exploring; use glossary vocabulary; surface ADR conflicts explicitly rather than overriding.

nodes.label: GitHub issues on Xeno828/delivery-value-dashboard via gh
nodes.norm_label: github issues on xeno828/delivery-value-dashboard via gh
nodes.rationale: All issue operations through the gh CLI; PRs are not a request surface; wayfinder maps are an issue labelled wayfinder:map with sub-issues and native dependencies.

nodes.label: Five canonical triage labels
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — label strings equal to the role names.

nodes.label: Durable series
nodes.rationale: Per-sprint rows recorded when each sprint closed, with observation time and status configuration. Not a cache; Jira stays authoritative. ADR 0015.

nodes.label: Reconstructed row
nodes.rationale: Re-derived after the fact for a sprint that closed before the app existed; a row with a different warrant, not a worse one.

nodes.label: Recorded row
nodes.rationale: A sprint's row written when it closed, when every figure was still observable.

nodes.label: CLAIM_FIELDS allow-list; problems_in_claim refuses rather than trims
nodes.norm_label: claim_fields allow-list; problems_in_claim refuses rather than trims
nodes.rationale: The same shape as the series store, for the same reason: nothing identifying an issue or a person.

nodes.label: issuesSeen: a row records how wide the view that produced it was
nodes.norm_label: issuesseen: a row records how wide the view that produced it was
nodes.rationale: A count naming no issue; without it the store cannot tell its own facts from one reader's version. A narrower view never replaces a row (recordable refuses, naming the numbers); a wider view corrects one, the single exception to ADR 0015's never-rewrite rule; a narrower reader is told so in a sentence and excluded from the unexplained-disagreement sentence.

nodes.label: ADR 0015: A durable series stores what Jira forgets, and re-derivation is a labelled fallback
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: a durable series stores what jira forgets, and re-derivation is a labelled fallback

nodes.label: ADR 0017: A forecast is logged as a count by a date, not as a promise about these items
nodes.norm_label: adr 0017: a forecast is logged as a count by a date, not as a promise about these items

nodes.label: ADR 0019: A recorded row is a fact about the board, not about the reader
nodes.norm_label: adr 0019: a recorded row is a fact about the board, not about the reader

nodes.label: The disclosure must name the right cause
nodes.norm_label: the disclosure must name the right cause
nodes.rationale: 'no sprint calendar' was printed for three different causes, including a calendar that was present. Three causes, three sentences. Most missing calendars were forge/src/jira.js sending no workingDays; the page now derives the day list under its own config.

nodes.label: The store holds counts, never issue text
nodes.norm_label: the store holds counts, never issue text
nodes.rationale: Nine numbers, a sprint name and two provenance fields. Reuses storage:app already granted for ADR 0014, and keeps item 4 from waiting on item 5's permission model: nothing in the store is an issue anyone could be denied sight of.

nodes.label: A sprint's row is written once when it closes and read thereafter
nodes.norm_label: a sprint's row is written once when it closes and read thereafter
nodes.rationale: The question asked of every field: if we throw this away, can Jira tell us again? A cache of an authoritative system is a second copy waiting to disagree, so the store holds only what cannot be recovered, with the observation date and the status configuration it was computed under. Lifting the six-sprint cap first was deferred behind the store.

nodes.label: Re-derivation is a labelled fallback, and disagreements are said aloud
nodes.norm_label: re-derivation is a labelled fallback, and disagreements are said aloud
nodes.rationale: A reconstructed row has a different warrant, not a worse one; recording a reconstruction as if observed would launder that warrant. Where a recorded row and a reconstruction disagree, say so — it is the only signal a status was recategorised under a year of history.

nodes.label: A claim's id is deterministic: context, day, percentile
nodes.norm_label: a claim's id is deterministic: context, day, percentile
nodes.rationale: Panel loads, the brief and a refreshing reader all produce the same forecast; without this the log holds one prediction eleven times and the Brier score looks excellent while measuring nothing.

nodes.label: A claim is resolved once, over (madeOn, horizon], and never rescored
nodes.norm_label: a claim is resolved once, over (madeon, horizon], and never rescored
nodes.rationale: Recounting later against a board whose issues have moved would quietly change a published score; an item finished the morning of the forecast was history, not prediction. Limits stated: four claims per forecast are correlated so n is overstated; work moved off the board resolves false; below ten resolved entries score_calibration refuses.

nodes.label: The forecast log gets two gates: publishing and resolving
nodes.norm_label: the forecast log gets two gates: publishing and resolving
nodes.rationale: A row is observed repeatedly and can be widened; a claim is made once and resolved once. The irreversible hazard is resolving a good claim from a view that cannot see the work, so a claim stays pending when the resolving view is narrower than the making view. Claims with no recorded width still resolve.

nodes.label: A recorded row is a fact about the board, not the reader
nodes.norm_label: a recorded row is a fact about the board, not the reader
nodes.rationale: The aggregate disclosure under issue-level security is accepted because what leaks is a count, the common project-level configuration discloses nothing, and the alternative (show a row only where the reader's view agrees) re-derives per reader and reintroduces the bug 4a fixed. The consequence with teeth: a row recorded by a narrow reader is not a disclosure but simply false.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.rationale: How past published forecasts scored against outcomes; without it a forecaster is unfalsifiable.

nodes.label: The four things Jira cannot tell us again
nodes.norm_label: the four things jira cannot tell us again
nodes.rationale: A published forecast; anything about a deleted issue; committedItems after sprint membership is stripped (predictability reconstructs as better than it was); and any figure whose meaning depends on the status categorisation in force at the time (started moves retroactively when a status is recategorised). Invocation cost is a fifth reason, labelled as an argument for caching, not recording.

nodes.label: A published forecast is logged as capacity claims: count, date, probability
nodes.norm_label: a published forecast is logged as capacity claims: count, date, probability
nodes.rationale: sprint_completion ('all of it by the 14th') cannot be resolved without recording which items were outstanding, i.e. issue keys — refused because it puts customer-identifiable data in an app-level store and puts 4c on item 5's critical path. capacity_to_target resolves from a count of completions in a window, needs no identity, and yields four claims per forecast, reachable for calibration bucketing this decade.

nodes.label: Published calibration score that stops probabilities
nodes.norm_label: published calibration score that stops probabilities
nodes.rationale: Every published probability is logged and scored; if the score degrades the agent stops quoting probabilities and says why.

nodes.label: Executive brief and team report from one set of facts
nodes.norm_label: executive brief and team report from one set of facts
nodes.rationale: Two documents, never one with a summary bolted on; under 400 words for leadership, issue keys throughout for the team.

nodes.label: Rollout: shadow, team report, exec brief, automate
nodes.norm_label: rollout: shadow, team report, exec brief, automate
nodes.rationale: Do not start at automate: a forecasting agent with no calibration history is a confident stranger; ten resolved predictions first.

nodes.label: Brier score over the forecast log
nodes.norm_label: brier score over the forecast log
nodes.rationale: Target <=0.12; above 0.20 the agent stops publishing probabilities in the body.

nodes.label: Agent guardrails
nodes.rationale: Never compute; never a single date; lead with probability against the reader's date; evidence tags; never attribute throughput to a person; never recommend longer hours; movement is the news; stale data first; publish the Brier score and stop above 0.20; never rank asks; an intake figure is never a commitment.

nodes.label: Backtest with non-overlapping windows and full horizons
nodes.norm_label: backtest with non-overlapping windows and full horizons
nodes.rationale: Only score cutoffs with a full horizon of real data (truncation made p50 coverage read 38%); never overlap windows (one slow fortnight counted ten times). Six windows is a smoke test, not calibration.

nodes.label: Reporting scope is not forecasting scope
nodes.norm_label: reporting scope is not forecasting scope
nodes.rationale: The facts pack counts only the reported period; the forecaster sees the whole file. Conflating them produced '89% complete' for a 55% sprint; tests/test_agent.py pins identical delivery figures.

nodes.label: Reporting and forecasting are two jobs with opposite failure modes
nodes.norm_label: reporting and forecasting are two jobs with opposite failure modes
nodes.rationale: Reporting's failure is a wrong number, forecasting's a confident number; both are computed by code and the agent narrates, diffs and frames a decision.

nodes.label: size_stability: drift and spread guard on item counting
nodes.norm_label: size_stability: drift and spread guard on item counting
nodes.rationale: Splitting work smaller raises throughput without output rising; a 30% cycle-time fall with a 20% throughput rise means splitting; p85/p50 above ~4 means items are not interchangeable. Forecasts marked provisional, never switched back to points.

nodes.label: Snapshot archive: facts packs, scope.json, forecast-log.json
nodes.norm_label: snapshot archive: facts packs, scope.json, forecast-log.json
nodes.rationale: A dashboard shows state; a report is about change. Without stored facts packs the agent only restates the dashboard, and without the forecast log it is unfalsifiable — a horoscope.

nodes.label: The agent never does arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Same question twice gives the same answer; a wrong figure is fixable in one line for everyone; the moment the agent computes a percentage nothing is auditable. Enforced structurally by tests asserting tools agree with the dashboard.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attributed to size vs delivery variability
nodes.norm_label: uncertainty attributed to size vs delivery variability
nodes.rationale: Three simulations (both varying, size frozen, throughput frozen) split the spread; size-driven sends the ask back to refinement, delivery-driven says the estimate was never the problem. 54% vs 10% on the demo.

nodes.label: What an ask is inside Jira (open product question)
nodes.norm_label: what an ask is inside jira (open product question)
nodes.rationale: Sequencing was never blocked on roadmap items 4 or 5 but on nobody deciding which Jira issue is an ask; ADR 0027 answered the value-basis half, the ask itself stayed open until 0028.

nodes.label: GET api/forecast?id=
nodes.rationale: Full forecast.py output plus sampled_from; items/date overrides echoed under asked and rejected with 400 rather than dropped; samples the whole team across all its sprints with remaining from the selected context; 400-working-day horizon reported as unfinished_fraction; calendar named in inputs.calendar.

nodes.label: GET api/sequence?id=
nodes.rationale: Runs intake.sequence() over data/asks/ for the board; bundle backend only, live Jira returns available: false because a sprint-at-a-time pull lacks completed epics and interruption rate. No value score is computed.

nodes.label: Bundle format (schemaVersion 2.0)
nodes.rationale: Additive to v1.0; contexts[], defaultContextId, issues[].contextId, byContext[id] with burndown/history/releases/dora. Each context's history contains only sprints up to and including itself so a past report does not leak the future.

nodes.label: Live mode via scripts/serve_live.py
nodes.rationale: Page probes api/contexts on load (skipped on file://); stubs fetched on selection only; server binds 127.0.0.1 and holds credentials in memory; the server's orgConfig wins because it computed the forecasts.

nodes.label: Interaction cost is flat in dataset size
nodes.norm_label: interaction cost is flat in dataset size
nodes.rationale: Measured by tests/perf.py: switching sprint ~23-39 ms from 22 to 5,538 issues; the ceiling is payload (2.8 MB at 66 boards), not rendering; scoping the sprint dropdown saves 0.0 ms.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: The page never queries Jira or Asana; data arrives as a bundle
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: the page never queries jira or asana; data arrives as a bundle

nodes.label: ADR 0023 Cross-team roll-up spans what the reader can see
nodes.norm_label: adr 0023 cross-team roll-up spans what the reader can see

nodes.label: Filtering by project, board and sprint (contexts and live mode)
nodes.norm_label: filtering by project, board and sprint (contexts and live mode)

nodes.label: Contexts fetched up front into a bundle
nodes.norm_label: contexts fetched up front into a bundle
nodes.rationale: A static HTML file has no MCP client, both tracker APIs reject cross-origin browser requests, and any embedded credential is readable by every recipient; bundling makes switching instant, offline and emailable. Proxying through a hosted service was rejected because it reintroduces the credential and infrastructure the single-file decision avoids.

nodes.label: Live mode: local server on 127.0.0.1
nodes.rationale: The deliberate escape hatch: a local server the user starts on purpose that the page discovers and pulls unbundled contexts from; degrades in one direction only.

nodes.label: Cross-team roll-up
nodes.rationale: Spans the boards this reader can see and names them, because the app reads the board list as the viewer and cannot know which boards it is not seeing; a count cannot be checked, three names can. Windows excluded because 14/30/90-day windows overlap.

nodes.label: Cross-team roll-up refuses to forecast
nodes.rationale: team_slice selects by team label and would forecast one team under a cross-team heading (the 1.8.0 19-day-read-77 failure); pooling teams assumes interchangeable throughput, which nothing establishes.

nodes.label: The page cannot call Jira or Asana itself
nodes.norm_label: the page cannot call jira or asana itself
nodes.rationale: CORS rejects browser-origin requests and any token in an HTML file is readable by everyone it is forwarded to; live data arrives via a script running where credentials already live, making the credential boundary explicit.

nodes.label: Size stability
nodes.rationale: Whether items are still interchangeable enough for counting to mean anything.

nodes.label: size_stability(): the interchangeable-items assumption is checked
nodes.norm_label: size_stability(): the interchangeable-items assumption is checked
nodes.rationale: Item forecasting assumes items are roughly interchangeable in size; that weakness is checked rather than trusted, looking for a team splitting work smaller and for cycle-time spread wide enough that counting loses meaning.

nodes.label: Agent intake mode's four standing rules
nodes.norm_label: agent intake mode's four standing rules
nodes.rationale: Run readiness first; report both scenarios; lead with the attribution, not the date; unachievable_at_any_priority is the headline whenever non-empty.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attribution (size vs delivery)
nodes.rationale: Three simulations: both varying, size frozen at median, throughput frozen at mean; partial spreads attributed proportionally. Answers which uncertainty to go and reduce; sends a vague ask to refinement and stops a team being told to tighten an estimate that was never the problem.

nodes.label: ADR 0006: Forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006: forecasts count items, never story points

nodes.label: Forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.norm_label: forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.rationale: Six sprints of points is six observations, which cannot support a distribution; the same sprints hold roughly sixty items. Item counting also cannot be inflated by estimating generously. Points remain a display toggle only.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo over item throughput, 20,000 seeded trials
nodes.norm_label: monte carlo over item throughput, 20,000 seeded trials
nodes.rationale: Six sprints give six point-observations but sixty items; zero-throughput days stay in the sample or the model never predicts a stall; fixed seed; scope growth sampled from scope.json and stated inline when absent.

nodes.label: Two forecaster fixes: dedupe by key, no default target
nodes.norm_label: two forecaster fixes: dedupe by key, no default target
nodes.rationale: team_slice() gathered three overlapping windows of one board so every issue arrived up to three times and the forecast came back 2.5x too fast; the window's endDate (today) was used as default target so 'will this land' answered 0% against a deadline nobody set. Also: forecast.build() passes 'or 10', inventing a ten-day sprint before recommend_commitment() can refuse — a live defect.

nodes.label: next_commitment's invented ten-day sprint
nodes.rationale: forecast.build passes 'or 10', so a dataset with no sprint dates got a commitment sized against a sprint nobody chose and recommend_commitment's correct refusal was unreachable.

nodes.label: A window supplies no default forecast target
nodes.norm_label: a window supplies no default forecast target
nodes.rationale: A window's endDate is today; passed as the default target, 'will this land in time' answered 0% about a deadline nobody set.

nodes.label: Candidate custom field
nodes.rationale: Text (Forge cannot declare a checkbox or select); Yes/Y/True case-insensitively; a site with a real checkbox points orgConfig.askField at it.

nodes.label: Issue schema (one row per issue)
nodes.rationale: key, summary, status, created required; started/resolved/dueDate, flagged, addedMidSprint, statusTransitions, businessValue, valueBasis, candidate, tshirt, type, storyPoints. No hours or overtime field, deliberately.

nodes.label: Intake sizing ladder: tshirt, reference-class, explicit
nodes.norm_label: intake sizing ladder: tshirt, reference-class, explicit
nodes.rationale: The rung is always declared and each prints its own caveat; two scenarios (earliest possible, realistic with queue and thinned throughput) always both, the difference reported as the cost of the queue in working days.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.norm_label: a t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.rationale: S/M/L/XL are quartiles of the epics this board has completed, so 'L' means 'like this board's third-quartile epics' and differs per board. A band selects which observed delivery an ask is compared against; it asserts no number, so an optimist's mistake is visible rather than an invisible inflation.

nodes.label: First answer, corrected: wipItems re-derives correctly
nodes.norm_label: first answer, corrected: wipitems re-derives correctly
nodes.rationale: history_row() counts in-progress from started/resolved dates that do not move, so the original premise (wipItems is irrecoverable) was false after 1.36.0 and the record was rewritten on the narrower, true case.

nodes.label: History rows are derived from dates at asOfDate, never current status
nodes.norm_label: history rows are derived from dates at asofdate, never current status
nodes.rationale: Read off current status a closed sprint reports everything ever finished and no WIP, so predictability improves the further back you look; shipped in the bundle path and both fixture generators. history_row() is the single implementation; live rows carry source recorded/reconstructed and differs.

nodes.label: Data bundle pill (Demo bundle - 3 boards x 6 sprints)
nodes.norm_label: data bundle pill (demo bundle - 3 boards x 6 sprints)

nodes.label: Header line (Project · Team · Sprint dates · data as at)
nodes.norm_label: header line (project · team · sprint dates · data as at)

nodes.label: Sprint selector (with current marker and item count)
nodes.norm_label: sprint selector (with current marker and item count)

nodes.label: Toolbar actions (Dark, Print, Export CSV, Load data)
nodes.norm_label: toolbar actions (dark, print, export csv, load data)

nodes.label: Runs on Atlassian badge
nodes.rationale: Egress disqualifies the app from the badge; forge eligibility reports it as two findings (remote services, egressing data). Originally described as 'the badge or a second implementation, nothing in between' — corrected by the 2026-09-01 amendment.

nodes.label: Forge bridge adapter (window.__DVD_BRIDGE__)
nodes.rationale: CommonJS, requires @forge/bridge inside a try because the SDK throws outside a Forge iframe; must be a classic script linked ahead of app.js because app.js decides at load which transport it has and an ES module is deferred.

nodes.label: ADR 0005: The tools compute; the agent only narrates
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005: the tools compute; the agent only narrates

nodes.label: ADR 0008: If we ship on Forge, Forge calls a hosted calculator
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008: if we ship on forge, forge calls a hosted calculator

nodes.label: Tools compute; the agent narrates
nodes.rationale: Every figure comes from metrics.py, forecast.py or intake.py and the agent quotes it, performing no arithmetic. When a number is wrong it is wrong in one Python file and fixed once; the moment the agent computes anything, no figure is auditable. The known liability is duplicated maths between tools and dashboard, made survivable by tests/test_agent.py.

nodes.label: Hosted calculator imports the Python tools unchanged
nodes.norm_label: hosted calculator imports the python tools unchanged
nodes.rationale: Forge runs Node and cannot execute agent/tools/. Porting the Monte Carlo to JavaScript is a second implementation (which ADR 0005 forbids) and dropping the forecast sells a delivery product without its forecast. Three measurements decided it: the tools are pure functions; a call is ~16 KB and does not grow with the customer; a dataset stripped of titles produces byte-identical figures, so no issue title leaves Atlassian.

nodes.label: Pyodide (CPython under WebAssembly) inside the Forge function
nodes.norm_label: pyodide (cpython under webassembly) inside the forge function
nodes.rationale: The third shape not considered originally: the existing Python unchanged under Pyodide inside the Forge function. Measured 2026-09-01: byte-identical figures to native CPython, no egress, ~10x slower, 6.8s cold load, IN.sequence 13.6s warm / 21s cold against a 25s resolver timeout. Decided later the same day in ADR 0031: the in-function route is taken and the calculator retired.

nodes.label: Pyodide in the Custom UI iframe (rejected)
nodes.norm_label: pyodide in the custom ui iframe (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Needs unsafe-eval in permissions.content.scripts, a major version carrying the September deadline; a hidden tab ran at less than half speed; and the weekly brief has no browser to run in.

nodes.label: One contract, two transports
nodes.rationale: Live mode asks four questions by route name and gets {ok, status, body} back over a same-origin GET (serve_live.py) or an invoke() left on window.__DVD_BRIDGE__ by the Forge adapter; the page cannot tell which it has. Body shapes are the contract; status is transport-level. Letting resolvers return their own shape and reshaping in the page was refused as one product behaving differently depending on how it was reached.

nodes.label: The resolver plays the fetcher's part, not the calculator's
nodes.norm_label: the resolver plays the fetcher's part, not the calculator's
nodes.rationale: statusCategory and started are absent over the bridge because deciding what a status means is organisation config; the resolver sends raw statusTransitions and the page decides. addedMidSprint IS read from the changelog because it needs no config and defaulting it to false would be a plausible wrong number (full marks for scope stability).

nodes.label: Figures enter by substitution and prose is checked for foreign numerals
nodes.norm_label: figures enter by substitution and prose is checked for foreign numerals
nodes.rationale: A model given numbers restates them and a restatement is a second copy that can disagree. Prose that introduces a numeral the tools did not produce fails the check and the brief is not sent — ADR 0005's contract kept rather than bent.

nodes.label: Connection check page (probe)
nodes.rationale: Not the product: exercises the three things a successful deploy does not prove, that the page can reach a resolver, that the resolver can read Jira with the declared scopes, and that the projection strips issue text before anything leaves the tenant.

nodes.label: Section 3: What would leave the tenant
nodes.norm_label: section 3: what would leave the tenant

nodes.label: Section 2: Reading a board by id
nodes.norm_label: section 2: reading a board by id
nodes.rationale: The app never lists boards here because enumerating them needs read:project:jira which nothing else in the probe requires.

nodes.label: Intake mode
nodes.rationale: Run readiness() first; always both scenarios; lead with uncertainty attribution; t-shirt dates are provisional; sequencing headlines unachievable_at_any_priority and offers no recommended order.

nodes.label: Capacity scenario
nodes.rationale: Exactly two, always together: earliest possible (a ceiling) and realistic (queued and interrupted).

nodes.label: Cost of the queue
nodes.rationale: Gap between the two scenarios in working days; the figure to quote because it prices what is in flight.

nodes.label: Queue ahead
nodes.rationale: Committed unfinished work an ask waits behind, excluding mid-sprint additions already modelled as interruption.

nodes.label: Readiness
nodes.rationale: Whether an ask carries enough to forecast at all, and which gaps widen the answer.

nodes.label: Sequence
nodes.rationale: An ordering of asks reported by what each costs the others; the ordering itself stays a human judgement, no priority score.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attribution
nodes.rationale: Split of spread between not knowing the size and normal delivery variability; says which is worth reducing.

nodes.label: The ask JSON format
nodes.rationale: id, title, requestedBy, team, problemStatement, successMeasure, sizing {method,size,basis}, valueEstimate {amount,basis,confidence}, neededBy, dependencies, assumptions.

nodes.label: The readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Required: title, team, sizing. Recommended: problemStatement, successMeasure, neededBy, valueEstimate, dependencies, assumptions, each absence reported with its consequence. Exists because an intake tool's failure mode is making an unchallenged ask look processed.

nodes.label: Intake brief template
nodes.rationale: Readiness verdict verbatim, size with basis and caveat, both scenarios, cost of the queue, what would narrow this, what it does not account for, value with basis; no priority score.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages publish job
nodes.rationale: workflow_dispatch only: the job copies all of data/ into a public site, so publishing is a per-run human decision, never a push.

nodes.label: Brief recipients card (#c-brief)
nodes.rationale: Sent by Jira's own notifications so nothing leaves the site; recipients are Jira accounts and groups, never email addresses; only a project administrator can change it.

nodes.label: Filter bar: person, epic, types, status, find, measure
nodes.norm_label: filter bar: person, epic, types, status, find, measure
nodes.rationale: Types is a details/checkbox disclosure rather than a custom listbox because native controls keep the keyboard and screen-reader behaviour the page is held to, and it changes what the page counts, not only what it lists.

nodes.label: Flow tile cards: c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd
nodes.norm_label: flow tile cards: c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd

nodes.label: Monte Carlo forecast card (#c-forecast) with When / How many / Sequence asks
nodes.norm_label: monte carlo forecast card (#c-forecast) with when / how many / sequence asks

nodes.label: Load data modal (#modal), three steps
nodes.rationale: Choose (drop, browse, paste, templates), map (column mapping table, sprint window, replace/merge radios), preview (stats, warnings, first rows, Apply).

nodes.label: Dashboard page shell (src/index.html)
nodes.rationale: The HTML skeleton build.py assembles with @@STYLES@@, @@SEED@@, @@APP@@ and @@IMPORT@@ placeholders into one self-contained file.

nodes.label: Tile grid (#grid)
nodes.rationale: c-exec, c-kpis, c-burn, c-dist, c-flow, c-age, c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd, c-pred, c-forecast, c-dora, c-load, c-value, c-rel, c-brief, c-risk; each chart card has a show-as-table toggle.

nodes.label: Top bar: source badge, health chip, theme, Tiles, Workflow, Print, Export, Load data
nodes.norm_label: top bar: source badge, health chip, theme, tiles, workflow, print, export, load data

nodes.label: Workflow chip button (#btn-workflow)
nodes.rationale: Hidden unless the config did not name every status the board uses; a permanent 'nothing was inferred' notice is furniture.

nodes.label: Import wizard (Load data)
nodes.rationale: Three steps, nothing applied until the reader has seen what was read; file is read in the browser, held in memory, never uploaded.

nodes.label: Replace or merge apply modes
nodes.rationale: Merge updates matching keys and only overwrites fields the file supplied, which is how a key,businessValue,valueBasis file layers on top of a Jira export.

nodes.label: Flow board window context (kind: window)
nodes.rationale: A rolling stretch of calendar days (14/30/90, 30 default) with no working-day list, so eight figures stop measuring a team against a boundary it never agreed to. A fixed set because two boards are comparable only if asked the same question. kind is sent by both transports, never inferred from the id.

nodes.label: Flow health composite
nodes.rationale: Same machine as sprint health (drop-and-name, re-weighting, half-weight floor) over flow efficiency 40%, blockers 30%, ageing 30%. Flow efficiency is load-bearing: without started it refuses outright rather than scoring hygiene as health.

nodes.label: The four flow tiles
nodes.rationale: Cycle time, ageing WIP, weekly throughput, cumulative flow. Shown by default only on a flow board, offered on any. CFD has three bands from status categories and says so; Little's Law is reconciled with no verdict drawn.

nodes.label: statusTransitions sent raw by the resolver
nodes.norm_label: statustransitions sent raw by the resolver
nodes.rationale: The resolver sends raw status transitions and the page decides what they mean under the config it holds, rather than computing started in a third implementation nobody can test against a tenant. Not capped: a truncated list would silently move a start date later.

nodes.label: orgConfig Jira project property on Forge
nodes.norm_label: orgconfig jira project property on forge
nodes.rationale: No file to read on Forge, so done statuses come from Jira's own status categories and the working week, holidays and sprint length from a project property named orgConfig, read with a scope the board picker already needs; the app never writes it. When absent the connection label says so.

nodes.label: Inferred statuses (orgConfig.inferredStatuses)
nodes.rationale: A status matching no rule falls through to the tracker's category, then a name heuristic, and is recorded and printed. Prevents the quiet failure where a new Awaiting sign-off column reads as To Do and the burndown flattens.

nodes.label: Organisation configuration (orgConfig)
nodes.rationale: Four things baked into the code and true of one company: done/inProgress statuses, working week, holidays, sprint length; later trendSprints, countSubtasks, countedTypes, valueFromHierarchy, askField, askFromHierarchy, sizeField.

nodes.label: Workflow chip and status mapping control
nodes.norm_label: workflow chip and status mapping control
nodes.rationale: Lists every status the data mentions with its current meaning and a control to change it. Applying writes into the dataset's own orgConfig.statuses and re-derives every figure; it edits the data, not the view, because a view toggle would have two readers disagreeing from one file and no browser storage to live in.

nodes.label: At most twelve asks on every transport
nodes.norm_label: at most twelve asks on every transport
nodes.rationale: Cost is cubic: 4 asks ~1 s, 8 ~7 s, 12 ~21 s, 16 ~48 s natively, ten times slower on Forge. intake.MAX_ASKS and intake.too_many_asks() refuse before reading the board; service and Forge quote that sentence. Twelve because three and a half minutes is as long as a reader should watch a tile.

nodes.label: Sequencing every ordering of the queue
nodes.norm_label: sequencing every ordering of the queue
nodes.rationale: Evaluates every ordering: when each ask lands at the 85th percentile and what it costs the others, and names first anything unachievable at any priority, which is the conversation that otherwise happens six weeks late.

nodes.label: Sequencing is cubic in the ask count
nodes.norm_label: sequencing is cubic in the ask count
nodes.rationale: Native 2 asks 0.17 s, 4 1.1 s, 8 7.0 s, 12 21 s, 16 48 s; fifty did not finish in ten minutes. Forge plain runtime ten times slower: 12 asks 209 s, 16 asks 479 s; twenty would not fit 900 s. Every earlier per-ask pricing, including ADR 0031's, is wrong by this shape.

nodes.label: Added-mid-sprint inferred from created date
nodes.rationale: Almost no tracker exports it; anything created after sprint start counts as added. Labelled as a proxy, but inferred rather than left blank because it drives the burndown scope line, the most useful thing over a stock Jira report.

nodes.label: All-numeric date disambiguation
nodes.rationale: Whole column scanned; a first part above 12 proves day-first. If nothing disambiguates it warns loudly rather than guessing, because a reversed format silently corrupts every elapsed-time figure.

nodes.label: Column mapping by synonym list
nodes.rationale: Headings matched against synonyms (Issue key/Key/Task ID/gid); every guess shown with an example and overridable. Only key, summary, status are required; everything else degrades with the preview naming which cards go blank.

nodes.label: Burndown and history row recomputed on upload
nodes.norm_label: burndown and history row recomputed on upload
nodes.rationale: Stale charts under fresh numbers is worse than no charts; only releases[] and dora{} carry forward because no tracker export contains them.

nodes.label: Sprint health refuses whole on a flow board
nodes.norm_label: sprint health refuses whole on a flow board
nodes.rationale: Pace (0.34) and scope stability (0.22) both need the clock; dropped, blockers and ageing hold 0.44, below the half-weight floor. What is left is hygiene, not whether anything lands.

nodes.label: Refuse in place versus not shown
nodes.norm_label: refuse in place versus not shown
nodes.rationale: A tile refuses in place when the condition can lift; it is not shown when it has no subject on this board and never will (burndown, commitment history, team load). Nothing dropped without being named in the context bar and the tile picker.

nodes.label: A bad config stops the run
nodes.norm_label: a bad config stops the run
nodes.rationale: Nothing is half-applied and nothing falls back; a typo silently reverting to a five-day week would move every forecast with nothing on screen saying so.

nodes.label: The config travels inside the data
nodes.norm_label: the config travels inside the data
nodes.rationale: Resolved once by the producer and written as a top-level orgConfig block; the page, metrics.py, forecast.py, intake.py and the live server all read it there. A config read separately by each consumer is a third opinion by a different route; the first symptom was 25% vs 22% flow efficiency for the same sprint. An emailed copy carries the calendar it was built with.

nodes.label: Two implementations, one behaviour
nodes.rationale: orgconfig.py is the reference; src/app.js mirrors it because the browser cannot call Python. tests/e2e.py asserts agreement under a non-default config since two implementations of Mon-Fri agree by accident. forge/src/jira.js mirrors validate() only, over shared fixtures.

nodes.label: Holidays affect working days only
nodes.rationale: Working week and holidays touch the Monte Carlo horizon, elapsed percentage and ideal line; reported elapsed time stays in calendar days. A holiday shortening an item's age would be the same lie as skipping weekends.

nodes.label: No priority score is computed
nodes.rationale: WSJF and kin multiply an unvalidated value by an unvalidated size and present the product as arithmetic. The delivery consequence of an ordering is computable and returned; the relative worth of asks is a judgement owned by people.

nodes.label: Team load: WIP and unplanned work from issue status
nodes.norm_label: team load: wip and unplanned work from issue status
nodes.rationale: The replacement metric: derived from issue status alone, so no effort data is needed. If a metric appears to need effort data it is the wrong metric.

nodes.label: Predictability card with recommended next commitment
nodes.norm_label: predictability card with recommended next commitment
nodes.rationale: History averaging ~37 points against 77 committed guarantees a 'failed' sprint; committed vs completed with hit rate and trailing average.

nodes.label: ADR 0003: The dashboard does not measure people
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003: the dashboard does not measure people

nodes.label: No hours, overtime, timesheet field; no ranking of individuals
nodes.norm_label: no hours, overtime, timesheet field; no ranking of individuals
nodes.rationale: A time-tracking field implies a regime the organisation does not operate and invites someone to fill it in; individual throughput comparison is a claim the data cannot support because throughput is a property of the system. An earlier version charted output-per-person against overtime and both were removed.

nodes.label: Health score with the method exposed on hover
nodes.norm_label: health score with the method exposed on hover
nodes.rationale: 'Overall Health: Amber' with no method cannot be challenged so it gets ignored; four weighted components each with weight, sub-score and sentence.

nodes.label: One completion figure from a single field
nodes.norm_label: one completion figure from a single field
nodes.rationale: The original showed Done 13, Tasks Done 15/22 and Work Complete 9/22 at once; a reader who notices stops trusting every other number.

nodes.label: Team load card replacing output-per-person and overtime
nodes.norm_label: team load card replacing output-per-person and overtime
nodes.rationale: The organisation does not operate overtime, so charting hours implied a regime that does not exist; output per person without a counterweight is a productivity-per-head number and this dashboard does not measure people. WIP and unplanned work from issue status answer the same question.

nodes.label: Waiting-vs-working elapsed time chart
nodes.rationale: Each closed item as one bar split into queue and active time; 22% active on the demo means 78% queueing, the largest and cheapest improvement, invisible when lead and cycle are two bars nobody subtracts.

nodes.label: Commitment recommended at the 85%-confidence item count
nodes.norm_label: commitment recommended at the 85%-confidence item count
nodes.rationale: Committing at the median misses half the time by construction and a team that misses half its commitments stops being believed; 11 items vs a median of 14 on the sample.

nodes.label: Context: one project + board + sprint
nodes.rationale: A bundle is a list of contexts plus their issues; pickers cascade project to board to sprint; each board offers an All N sprints roll-up where burndown and releases refuse.

nodes.label: Window context ids on flow boards (win:14d/30d/90d)
nodes.norm_label: window context ids on flow boards (win:14d/30d/90d)
nodes.rationale: Only the three offered spellings are accepted; win:030d is refused rather than clamped because the page keys on the string. A window is not a clock and never carries workingDays.

nodes.label: Burndown with a scope line and mid-sprint callout
nodes.norm_label: burndown with a scope line and mid-sprint callout
nodes.rationale: Separates 'this team is slow' from 'this team was given more work' — opposite conversations the original merged.

nodes.label: Burndown carries both units, always
nodes.rationale: A burndown only in story points puts the toggle and the item-forecasting agent in different units by construction; recalculated from issues on upload.

nodes.label: orgConfig.inferredStatuses
nodes.rationale: A record of where the assumptions ran out: each unnamed status, what it was read as, and whether from the tracker's category or the words in its name. Exists because an 'Awaiting sign-off' column read as To Do makes a flat burndown that looks like a team delivering nothing. workflowSetBy: reader suppresses it.

nodes.label: started, recovered from the changelog
nodes.rationale: Not a field Jira keeps; the earliest transition into a status the current orgConfig calls in-progress (earliest, not first, because Jira's changelog is unordered). A producer that cannot resolve it sends statusTransitions; a bundle carries started outright and the raw list is ignored so one issue cannot get two answers. Recategorising a status moves every past sprint's started retroactively.

nodes.label: Units: items by default; calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.norm_label: units: items by default; calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.rationale: Items cannot be inflated by estimating generously and are the forecaster's unit; points remain the better lens for whether scope growth mattered. Elapsed time in calendar days, simulation in working days, every figure carrying its unit.

nodes.label: Calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.norm_label: calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.rationale: Found by a test: facts pack and dashboard disagreed on flow efficiency 25% vs 22% purely on this. Holidays shorten simulated time only; shortening the working week can drop a board under the refusal threshold, and the refusal is the right output.

nodes.label: Delivery consequence of an ordering
nodes.rationale: What is genuinely computable: what each sequence of asks costs the others in working days. Relative worth stays with the people accountable for it.

nodes.label: NEVER_SEND / FREE_TEXT_FIELDS boundary
nodes.rationale: valueBasis is refused at the calculator door so a currency amount arrives with no issue key and no sentence; the rule predates the field.

nodes.label: Value Basis custom field (free text)
nodes.rationale: Second jira:customField; a minor version (7.2.0). Separate from the description so 'no basis recorded' stays sayable for readiness().

nodes.label: ADR 0004: Intake returns delivery consequence, never a priority score
nodes.norm_label: adr 0004: intake returns delivery consequence, never a priority score

nodes.label: ADR 0027 A value basis is prose carried to a reader
nodes.norm_label: adr 0027 a value basis is prose carried to a reader

nodes.label: No WSJF or value-over-effort priority score
nodes.norm_label: no wsjf or value-over-effort priority score
nodes.rationale: Every score of that family multiplies an unvalidated value estimate by an unvalidated size estimate and presents the product as arithmetic, laundering a judgement into a number that is hard to argue with. The rejection is the decision and it is expected to be re-proposed.

nodes.label: A value basis is prose, never an input
nodes.norm_label: a value basis is prose, never an input
nodes.rationale: Nothing parses, compares or ranks it; an enumerated basis is one join from a table of weights, i.e. ADR 0004's priority score by the back door. A sentence is falsifiable, a category is not.

nodes.label: Value figure as a floor with a basis line per item
nodes.norm_label: value figure as a floor with a basis line per item
nodes.rationale: '$86,000 delivered' with no methodology loses credibility in one meeting; label it an estimate, show each basis, count items with no estimate.

nodes.label: Sequencing returns consequences, never a score
nodes.norm_label: sequencing returns consequences, never a score
nodes.rationale: Anything missing its date in every ordering is reported first; no WSJF or weighted score because they multiply two unvalidated estimates and present the product as arithmetic.

nodes.label: data/demo-intake-bundle.json
nodes.rationale: The main demo bundle has no finished epics, so make_intake_demo.py writes a separate bundle with 16 delivered epics dated before the demo window so the delivery forecaster's trailing throughput is untouched.

nodes.label: No text from the page reaches Jira
nodes.norm_label: no text from the page reaches jira
nodes.rationale: The only caller-supplied input is a context id; parseContextId refuses anything not canonical, so the app can issue only three date pairs per board built by the resolver from its own clock. Justifies read:jql:jira.

nodes.label: A parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.norm_label: a parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.rationale: Filtering in the producer was rejected because it discards the raw issues and a config change would need a refetch; the rule is applied where figures are made, in Python and mirrored in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Ask
nodes.rationale: A product request being weighed against others; a document in data/asks/ or an epic marked candidate. Declared, not inferred from tickets.

nodes.label: Band
nodes.rationale: The S/M/L/XL on an epic; selects a quartile of the board's completed epics and asserts no number. ADR 0029.

nodes.label: Candidate
nodes.rationale: An issue somebody declared under consideration; a state, not a type, untrue only when the declarer takes it back. ADR 0028.

nodes.label: Epic
nodes.rationale: Parent grouping; the sample unit for sizing an ask once nearly complete, and an ask itself when declared a candidate.

nodes.label: Reference class
nodes.rationale: The board's completed epics used as the sample; whole class with no band, one quartile with one.

nodes.label: Sizing method
nodes.rationale: t-shirt, reference class or explicit; recorded with every forecast because it bounds trust.

nodes.label: T-shirt scale
nodes.rationale: S/M/L/XL bands from one board's own completed epics in items; never organisation-wide.

nodes.label: Candidacy is decided in the resolver, costing a JS mirror
nodes.norm_label: candidacy is decided in the resolver, costing a js mirror
nodes.rationale: Deciding it in the calculator would send the unreadable answers ('Maybe', 'ask Priya') — customer free text — out of the tenant. What crosses is id, sizing method, amount and date; the resolver joins title and basis back by id (a lookup, like reattach).

nodes.label: Forecasting rules
nodes.rationale: Never a single date; lead with probability against the existing date; items not points; commit at the 85% figure from recommend_commitment; check size_stability; state the scope assumption; never forecast an unstarted item's duration; never name a person.

nodes.label: Issue
nodes.rationale: One row of tracker data, the atomic unit. Avoid ticket, card, task.

nodes.label: Item
nodes.rationale: An issue counted as one regardless of size; the only unit a forecast uses.

nodes.label: Point
nodes.rationale: Story-point estimate; a display lens, never a forecasting input.

nodes.label: Import problem issue template
nodes.rationale: Asks for the header row only and one date sample, never issue data, so a bug report cannot carry real issue titles.

nodes.label: Commitment recommendation
nodes.rationale: Next-sprint item count from recent throughput; an input to a conversation. Refuses on a flow board for want of a cadence.

nodes.label: Interruption rate
nodes.rationale: Unplanned share of all work taken on, per board, used to thin the throughput series in a forecast.

nodes.label: Throughput
nodes.rationale: Items completed per working day sampled across a trailing window; zero days are part of the distribution. Shown per calendar week as a series.

nodes.label: Unplanned work
nodes.rationale: Items that arrived after planning; the other half of team load.

nodes.label: Work in progress
nodes.rationale: Started but unfinished at period end; half of team load, from status alone.

nodes.label: Cost of the existing queue
nodes.rationale: The number to quote: the price of everything already in flight in working days at the 85th percentile, converting 'why can't you start now' into arithmetic.

nodes.label: Two capacity scenarios, always both
nodes.rationale: Earliest possible (dedicated capacity) and realistic (queued behind committed work, throughput thinned at the measured interruption rate as a stochastic series, not a multiplier). Two dates make the gap the subject.
